describes: app-import.js §16 — the progressive load / import engine
contract: The import engine is the app's only inbound path, and what it produces is a SEQUENCE, not a value: reset, prepare, then per train append -> warm -> draw -> list -> progress, then one authoritative render, then finish. A port that lands on the same store having reported progress in a different order is a port whose progressive load looks wrong on screen and whose partial states cannot be reasoned about. The per-train step is the composition of BOTH front doors — normalizeImportedTrain, then makeUniqueTrainId, then validateTrain on the exported shape — and that composition accepts things neither door accepts alone.

cases.label: the committed jp store, replaced from a parsed value
the committed tw store, replaced from a parsed value
the committed jp store, replaced from JSON text
cases.note: the text door differs from the value door in three ways at once: it always persists each step, its final bar counts `total` rather than the trains that actually appended, and its status line comes BEFORE that bar instead of after.

cases.label: an empty array as the document
no document at all
cases.note: THROWS, and the comment above the code says it should not. `store || { trains: [] }` synthesises a store with an array `trains` and therefore takes the STORE branch of parseImportedCanonicalStore — where the synthesised object has no schema_version and is rejected. The empty-store path the fallback exists to reach can only be reached by passing an object that already carries schema_version, so a null store aborts the replacement instead of clearing the screen.

cases.label: replaceTrainStoreFromJsonText while an import is already running
cases.note: the guard returns early WITHOUT clearing importInProgress and WITHOUT announcing importFinished — the run that owns the flag still owns it. The text door returns undefined where the other two return a count.

cases.label: replaceTrainStoreFromStoreProgressive while an import is already running
cases.note: the guard returns early WITHOUT clearing importInProgress and WITHOUT announcing importFinished — the run that owns the flag still owns it. The text door returns undefined where the other two return a count.

cases.label: importCanonicalStoreAppendProgressive while an import is already running
cases.note: the guard returns early WITHOUT clearing importInProgress and WITHOUT announcing importFinished — the run that owns the flag still owns it. The text door returns undefined where the other two return a count.

cases.label: a stop whose name is a number
cases.note: stopName returns the raw value as a truthiness test, and canonicalStopShape then spells it with String() — so the validator only ever sees "12".

cases.label: ride_segment is the string "false"
cases.note: a non-empty string is truthy, so this RIDES the segment it says it does not.

cases.label: route_sections is the number 0
cases.note: validateTrain skips a falsy-but-present route_sections entirely; the import path does not skip it, it REPLACES it with [] — so the two doors disagree about what the train even contains.

cases.label: route_policy is the number 0
cases.note: same falsy-skip in the validator, same replacement with the canonical defaults on import.

cases.label: line_names is null
cases.note: `x || []` turns a null array into an empty one.
cases.input: {"schema_version":"1.3","trains":[{"id":"lean_001","number":"1M","origin":"東京","destination":"品川","stops":[{"name":"東京","departure":"08:00","ride_segment":true},{"name":"品川","arrival":"08:08"}],"route_sections":[{"from":"東京","to":"品川","line_names":null}]}]}

cases.label: a four-digit station code that is a number
cases.note: rejected — but on its LENGTH, not its type: the grammar wants six digits, and 3770 spells four of them.
cases.error: Train 1 stop 1: n02_station_code must be a six-digit N02_005c, a TDX StationUID, or null.

cases.label: a six-digit station code that is a number
cases.note: ACCEPTED: stationCodeSystem coerces with String() before matching, so a JSON number is a valid N02_005c. The import path keeps it a number all the way into the canonical store — which is the one place the Swift model cannot follow, because Stop.n02StationCode is a String?.

cases.label: no stop is ridden
cases.note: jsonspec §8.6.4 notwithstanding, nothing checks it: this validates, exports, and draws nothing.

cases.label: the clock runs backwards
cases.note: no two stops are ever compared.

cases.label: times that are not times
cases.note: normalizeNullableTime only trims; nothing parses a time.

cases.label: direction is a number
cases.note: accepted by both doors — and normalizeImportedTrain keeps the NUMBER, because `train.direction || "down"` never coerces.

cases.label: visible is the string "yes"
cases.note: the test is `!== false`, so every value except false means visible.

cases.label: visible is 0
train_type is a number
cases.note: THE asymmetry: validateTrain rejects a numeric train_type outright, but normalizeImportedTrain has already coerced it to "" by the time the validator runs — so the import engine ACCEPTS what the validator refuses.

cases.label: an id that is not in the documented charset
cases.note: REJECTED, though normalizeImportedTrain never applies TRAIN_ID_PATTERN: the pattern arrives with the second door.
cases.error: Train 1: id must match ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$ (letters, digits, "_" and "-").

cases.label: an id with surrounding whitespace
cases.note: ACCEPTED and silently trimmed. makeUniqueTrainId runs between the two doors and trims the base, so the id validateTrain sees is not the id the document contained.

cases.label: an id that is only whitespace
cases.note: ACCEPTED as the id "train": a whitespace-only base is falsy after trimming, and makeUniqueTrainId's second fallback catches it.

cases.label: a stop whose name is null
cases.note: the import whitelist's guard is `"name" in stop`, so this passes door one and is caught by door two.
cases.error: Train 1 stop 1: name is required.

cases.label: a stop row that is null
cases.note: one of the three inputs that CRASH validateTrain with a TypeError — but not through this door: normalizeImportedStop rejects it as a plain Error first, so the crash is unreachable from an import.
cases.error: Each stop must be an object.

cases.label: a route_sections row that is null
cases.note: likewise converted to an Error by normalizeImportedRouteSection before the validator can dereference it.
cases.error: Each route_section must be an object.

cases.label: a stop_type outside the enum
cases.note: the import path never consults STOP_TYPES — the validator does, and rejects it.
cases.error: Train 1 stop 1: stop_type must be one of origin / passenger_stop / pass_through / operational_stop / destination.

cases.label: style is a string
cases.note: `train.style?.color` on a string is undefined, so the default colour wins.

cases.label: an unsupported train key
cases.error: Train contains unsupported field: nickname.

cases.label: route_geometry, the removed field
cases.error: Train contains unsupported field: route_geometry.

manifestCases.label: a well-formed manifest, with parts_api attached
the fetch fails
manifestCases.note: an unreachable manifest memoises as null and is never retried.

manifestDatesCases.label: dates is an array
manifestDatesCases.note: an array IS an object, so this reaches the filter and its indices are the keys.

manifestDatesCases.label: dates is an array OF arrays
manifestDatesCases.note: and the indices are then real answers: "0" is a day whose list is non-empty. A port that reads keys off an array but cannot read VALUES back off one returns [] here and looks right on every other case.

manifestDatesCases.label: empty and non-array day lists are dropped
the empty-string key is dropped
manifestDatesCases.note: precompute files undated trains under "", and `key &&` is what keeps that bucket out of the boot's random-day choice.

manifestDatesCases.label: keys sort by UTF-16 code unit, not by locale
manifestDatesCases.note: Array.prototype.sort with no comparator compares code units, so "2026-1-3" sorts before "2026-12-03" and both before "2026-2-03".

partCases.label: three good parts
partCases.note: the window is index..index+4 INCLUSIVE — five parts, not four — clamped to the last index, and each part is fetched exactly once because the in-flight map is consulted before a new request is made.

partCases.note: one retry, then null — a single flaky request skips one train instead of aborting the whole boot.

partCases.note: NOTE the prefetch: part-000's single allowed failure is consumed by the prefetch issued for it, so the retry the cursor makes is a second request.

seedCases.label: unsolvable AND carrying features
seedCases.note: unsolvable wins: the negative cache is seeded and the features are dropped.

seedCases.label: unsolvable is the string "true"
seedCases.note: the test is `=== true`, so a truthy non-boolean falls through to the features branch.

seedCases.label: a cache_key that is a number
seedCases.note: `typeof !== "string"` rejects it before the features are looked at.

sampleNameCases.label: the whole sample
sampleNameCases.note: a null date loads manifest.parts and lands on the combined 全部 view.

sampleNameCases.label: a day the manifest does not have
sampleNameCases.note: falls back to the WHOLE sample rather than loading nothing — but the mode still says sample-single, because the mode is decided by the argument and the names by the manifest.

sampleNameCases.label: a day whose list is empty
sampleNameCases.note: an empty array IS an array, so this loads zero parts — sampleManifestDates would never have offered this day, but an explicit request reaches it.
